The Problem

You already know wholesaling works. You just don't have a system — or a deadline.

You've watched the videos, saved the PDFs, and told yourself "this month I'll actually do it." Then the leads pile up, the numbers never get verified, and the contract sits unsigned. Rachel's challenge replaces intention with a plan you do one action a day — the same actions that put assignment fees in real mailboxes.

The Solution

Exactly what's inside the 30-Day Challenge

Buy Box & Fee Goal

Define the deal you'll actually pursue and the exact assignment fee you need to hit your $3,500 target in one transaction.

About Rachel

Your coach is a deal-doer, not a course-seller

Rachel coaches real-estate assignment-of-contract — getting a property under an assignable contract and assigning it to an end buyer for a fee, never owning it. The method only works when it's done ethically, transparently, and with real numbers. That's the standard she holds every day of the challenge.

Her coaching style is direct: verify the comp, confirm the motivation, check the contract with qualified counsel, and disclose everything to the buyer. No scripted hype. No fabricated comps. Just a repeatable path to your first assignment fee.

FAQ

Questions, answered straight

Is assigning contracts legal in my state?

Assignment of contract is legal in most states, but rules differ. Always confirm with a qualified local real-estate attorney or title/escrow professional before marketing, signing, or assigning. The challenge is educational, not legal advice.

Do I need a real-estate license?

Generally no — assigning a contract positions you as a private party, not a licensed broker, in most jurisdictions. But state rules vary, and some compensation structures require a license. Verify locally with qualified counsel.

Do I need money to start?

A small marketing budget helps, but the challenge centers on free and low-cost sources: driving for dollars, motivated-seller outreach, your network, and permission-based conversations.

What if I don't hit $3,500 in 30 days?

$3,500 is a target, not a promise — your results depend on your market, activity, and follow-through. You keep every playbook and script forever, and Pro/Platinum members keep coaching until that first fee lands.

How much time does it take daily?

45–90 minutes a day for missions, outreach, and deal work. The roadmap is built for evenings and weekends, so you can run it alongside a job.

Can I cancel anytime?

Yes. Memberships are monthly, and you can cancel anytime from your Stripe billing portal. No long-term contracts.

database/BILLING-SETUP.md:
# Rachel durable billing repair

Implemented code is a release candidate, not a live verified billing service. No production schema/configuration/account change or real payment was performed. Thirteen local mocked tests exercise security gates, stable retries, webhook signature handling, durable event acceptance rollback, latest-state reconciliation, refunds and usage denials. Real PostgreSQL concurrency/rollback, Stripe sandbox lifecycle and production end-to-end acceptance are still required; mocked SQL is not proof of database correctness.

## Configure and migrate in a test environment

1. Provision or select the authorized Neon PostgreSQL database. Apply `database/billing.sql` using its protected connection. Database role must have rights to the four app tables; never expose DATABASE_URL. Use separate test/live databases when feasible (rows also include billing_mode). Set database UTC; application transactions explicitly set UTC.
2. Configure DATABASE_URL, WorkOS AuthKit credentials/callback, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_BILLING_MODE=test, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and price IDs STRIPE_PRICE_STARTER/PRO/PLATINUM. Server verifies USD recurring monthly prices of 499/1999/9999 cents, interval_count 1. Live mode explicitly requires `STRIPE_BILLING_MODE=live` and an sk_live secret; test is the default. Mode/config mismatches fail closed.
3. Serve hosted checkout only. Frontend sends authenticated same-origin POST `/api/checkout` with `{tier,ui:'hosted',attempt:'UUID'}`. Retain the UUID for retries of that same purchase; server binds it to authenticated user/tier. No arbitrary price, customer or redirect is accepted. Creation binds checkout and subscription metadata to WorkOS user and app. Display billing consent/terms before the user intentionally submits; do not automatically create checkout on page load.
4. Configure the Stripe webhook `/api/billing/webhook` with raw unmodified request bytes. Netlify must set req.rawBody before any JSON parsing. Vercel export disables bodyParser and reads bounded raw bytes. Subscribe at least checkout.session.completed and async success/failure, customer.subscription.created/updated/deleted, invoice.paid/payment_failed, charge.refunded, charge.dispute.created/updated/closed. Event types outside this handler's subscription/refund actions are durably accepted without granting access.
5. Stripe customer portal settings must enable allowed cancellation/billing controls. `/api/billing/portal` is authenticated, strict same-origin POST and resolves only the stored server-selected customer; no client customer ID accepted. Publish the root-owned Manage billing action and policy copy. Stripe dashboard/account eligibility and actual portal configuration still need testing.
6. Wrap paid chat/TTS/LiveKit handlers in `requireAccess(req,res,{feature:'chat'|'tts'|'voice'})`; it returns the authenticated user or null after sending the denial. For membership read/write services use `consume:false`. Root owns route integration and accurate UI promises.

## Access and operational policy

Only exactly one mapped active subscription, matching configured monthly plan and a latest invoice marked paid, can unlock service. Trialing/incomplete/past_due/unpaid/paused/canceled and provider/database errors deny access. End-of-term cancellation retains service while provider status remains active and term has not expired. The handler retrieves latest subscription state inside a database member-row lock rather than trusting delayed event snapshots. Retired price active flags alone do not revoke an already purchased mapped subscription; its currency/amount/interval still must match. Multiple mapped active subscriptions require review.

Any partial/full charge refund or dispute event blocks this customer from all paid services pending manual review. This intentionally conservative policy also blocks on dispute.closed even if won. An operator must reconcile charge/subscription records, decide the documented policy outcome and only then authorize clearing `blocked`; there is no user-facing unblock API. Cancellation/refund effects must be verified in sandbox; financial reconciliation and settlement reports remain outside this code.

Daily UTC request quotas are 30 chat requests, 30 TTS requests and one voice token issuance per paid user. Reservation occurs before provider work; provider failure consumes the allowance, avoiding automatic uncertain-cost retry. Request quotas are not monetary ceilings and a voice token expiry does NOT disconnect an existing room. Keep voice disabled until the real worker/server enforces a five-minute session cap, can stop billing work on cancellation and has a verified budget/usage dashboard. Do not advertise guaranteed daily outgoing calls until the real scheduler/call worker and consent/destination mappings pass acceptance.

## Recovery and retry durability

PostgreSQL rows are the sole entitlement/usage source; there is no memory fallback. Row locks serialize customer mapping, checkout and reconciliation. Checkout commits a pending attempt before creating provider objects; duplicate attempt returns the saved session. A pending attempt prevents a new distinct attempt for one hour. The provider session receives the fixed reservation expiry and deterministic hashed key. If recovery is delayed into the last 30 minutes of its expiry without a saved result, it fails closed for review instead of issuing ambiguous work. A completed session must not be reused as proof of paid access: account status re-verifies provider membership.

Customer creation has a durable start time and stable hashed idempotency key. If mapping is still absent after 23 hours, retries stop for manual reconciliation before the provider's idempotency retention may lapse. Review and repair the authoritative provider customer mapping, not blindly reset the clock. Provider success followed by database failure can leave an object requiring reconciliation, but it cannot automatically advance to a fresh operation key.

Webhook event IDs are unique per mode. Acceptance and entitlement updates commit in one transaction; any provider/storage error rolls back and returns an error for Stripe retry. Duplicates return success after prior durable commit. Follow Stripe delivery dashboard and application error rates; retry failures are not swallowed. Schedule a read-only reconciliation job and monitor outstanding webhook deliveries, blocked customers and checkout uncertainty. Root owns actual scheduler creation; this document does not imply one exists.

## External release blockers

Authorized test schema deployment, protected secret configuration, actual price verification and live-mode authorization; real Postgres simultaneous request tests; signed Stripe test checkout/renewal/cancellation/refund/dispute/duplicate/out-of-order events; per-request provider cost/usage accounting; support/refund operations; five-minute worker enforcement; exact deployed commit/config binding; QAI paid/unpaid browser acceptance. No paid release PASS follows from code alone.

Official implementation references checked 2026-10-09 UTC: https://docs.stripe.com/api/checkout/sessions/create , https://docs.stripe.com/api/subscriptions/retrieve , https://docs.stripe.com/webhooks , https://docs.stripe.com/customer-management . Neon connection documentation https://neon.com/docs/connect/connect-from-any-app could not be fetched in this run; use verified provider connection-string/TLS settings when configuring. Keep TLS certificate verification enabled; the application does not disable it.
